bibl.title: Memory processes underlying long-term semantic priming

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Evidence from the two experiments suggests that long-term semantic priming effects are due to different memory processes for different semantic content.

span.label: long-term semantic priming
span.quote: In two experiments, we used different semantic content – word meaning versus category membership – to investigate the mechanisms accountable for long-term semantic priming.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Two priming experiments were designed to be as structurally similar as possible, with one containing category exemplar and feature stimuli and the other containing synonym and antonym stimuli.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The memory process supporting long-term priming shifts with how the relevant part of semantic memory is organised associatively
span.note: status: the paper's own words: we propose that
span.quote: we propose that the memory processes underlying long-term semantic priming effects differ as a function of the associative organization of semantic memory for the stimulus domain in use.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because categories are hierarchically organised under a shared label, a prime trial and a target trial repeat the very same label-retrieval and comparison operation, and that repetition is what speeds the target
span.quote: The repetition of this operation performed relative to the same category is likely to play a substantial role in the target trial facilitation compared to unprimed category trials.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Synonyms and antonyms have no superordinate label to re-retrieve, so priming there can only come from incremental strengthening of the abstract semantic features the words share
span.quote: depends on increments of strength in abstract semantic representations that partially overlap for synonyms and antonyms.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Operation-specific facilitation appears only in the category domain because of the hierarchical structure of category knowledge
span.quote: That is, operation-specific facilitation is uniquely found in the category domain because of the hierarchical structure of that knowledge.

span.label: The evaluation operations manipulated in the two experiments were not equivalent, so the operations themselves - not the semantic content - may have produced the difference in priming.
span.quote: Despite these efforts, it is possible that the nature of the operations used in Experiment 1 lent themselves to priming differences more than those used in Experiment 2, irrespective of the semantic content.

span.label: The manipulation of content evaluations could not be made isomorphic across the two experiments.
span.quote: First, the manipulation of content evaluations was not isomorphic across experiments.

span.label: Participants may have used one shared strategy for both synonym and antonym decisions, and the authors have no data to rule this out.
span.quote: We do not have evidence to support this conclusion, but it is clear that the synonym/antonym decisions likely represent similar cognitive operations and thus the difference in priming magnitude between these operations is non-existent.

span.label: The question is not settled by these two experiments and needs a wider range of stimuli, task demands and prime-target lags.
span.quote: A full resolution of this issue will require further evidence of semantic priming effects stemming from a greater variety of stimuli and task demands across a range of prime-target lags.

span.label: a separate set of 64 stimulus groups was built to serve as filler trials, separating prime trials from target trials
span.note: eliminates: that the priming effect is carried by adjacency - that prime and target are simply consecutive
span.quote: A separate set of 64 stimulus groups was created to serve as practice examples and filler trials for separating prime and target trials.

span.label: long-term semantic priming
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: semantic memory representations
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: memory for prior cognitive operations
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: word meanings
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: category membership
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: **TWO RIVAL MECHANISMS, TWENTY YEARS APART, STATED AS ALTERNATIVES:** `The first explanation is that long-term semantic priming effects rely upon the INCREMENTAL STRENGTHENING OF ABSTRACT SEMANTIC MEMORY REPRESENTATIONS. The second explanation is that long-term priming is the result of MEMORY FOR PRIOR COGNITIVE OPERATIONS.` **One says the concept got stronger; the other says the subject remembers what they did.** They are not degrees of the same account - one is about the representation and the other about the act - and until this paper the literature had been arguing which
span.quote: The first explanation is that long-term semantic priming effects rely upon the incremental strengthening of abstract semantic memory representations. The second explanation is that long-term priming is the result of memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: **AND THE ANSWER IS NEITHER - IT IS BOTH, SPLIT BY CONTENT:** `Long-term semantic priming of WORD MEANINGS was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of CATEGORY MEMBERSHIP was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations.` **A dissociation inside a phenomenon the field had treated as one thing**, told apart only by varying the material while holding the task constant. This is the corpus's own thesis arriving as somebody else's empirical result: one term, two mechanisms, and no way to see it without the manipulation
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: **THE DESIGN POINT IS THE SAME ONE erb2019 MAKES, ONE RECORD APART:** `the priming tasks were designed to be AS SIMILAR AS POSSIBLE, while the PREVIOUS EVIDENCE CAME FROM DIFFERENT TASKS that could have been responsible for the difference in findings.` The earlier literature compared mechanisms across experiments differing in more than the variable of interest. **Two consecutive records now say a body of results is uninterpretable because a confound was not held constant** - erb2019 about associative-priming overlap, this about task differences - and neither is a critique paper. Both are ordinary empirical papers that had to clear the ground before they could ask anything
span.quote: the priming tasks were designed to be as similar as possible, while the previous evidence came from different tasks that could have been responsible for the difference in findings

span.label: **AND THE ASYMMETRY IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN NAMED - A CATEGORY HAS A LABEL AND A SYNONYM PAIR DOES NOT.** Evaluating whether roses and carnations share a category activates `flower`, and the next trial repeats that same evaluation against that same label; but `Deciding that placid rather than chaotic has a similar meaning to tranquil DOES NOT OCCUR WITH REFERENCE TO AN OVERARCHING CATEGORY LABEL with which the synonyms are exemplars.` **There is no operation to repeat, so only strengthening is left.** The mechanism is derived from the structure of the material rather than fitted to the result, which is what makes it a prediction for the next study rather than a description of this one
span.quote: Deciding that placid rather than chaotic has a similar meaning to tranquil does not occur with reference to an overarching category label with which the synonyms are exemplars

span.label: builds-on → Woltz (2010) and Woltz et al. (2015)
span.quote: This is consistent with findings by Woltz (2010) and Woltz et al. (2015).

span.label: replicates → Woltz and Was (2007)
span.quote: Our findings support the conclusion that semantic priming of category comparisons is partly operationspecific, and this is similar to findings by Woltz and Was (2007).

span.label: contradicts → Woltz and Was (2007)
span.quote: This differs from earlier findings by Woltz and Was (2007), and suggests that some facilitation reflects a generalized increase in availability of category information regardless of category operation.

span.label: semantic memory representations —causes→ long-term semantic priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **ONE OF TWO MECHANISMS, AND THE EDGE IS ONLY TRUE IN ONE CONTENT DOMAIN.** The quote says `Long-term semantic priming OF WORD MEANINGS was dependent on` this - not long-term priming generally. Read alone this edge overstates; read with its twin below it is the paper's finding. **Q-804's `moderates` gap again**: the content domain conditions which mechanism applies and there is no way to say so on an edge, so it is said in the note and quoted whole in the second sense. Weight 0.9.
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: memory for prior cognitive operations —causes→ long-term semantic priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE OTHER MECHANISM, on the same sentence and at the same weight, and the pair is the point. This one holds for CATEGORY MEMBERSHIP only - and the fourth sense explains why, from the structure of the material: a category has a label that the same evaluation is repeated against, and a synonym pair has nothing to repeat. **Recording either edge without the other would turn a dissociation into a claim about the phenomenon as a whole**, which is the thing this paper exists to refute.
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: word meanings —contrasted-with→ category membership
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE CONTRAST IS THE INSTRUMENT.** These two content domains are not being compared for their own sake - varying them while holding the task constant is what made the two mechanisms separable, and the previous literature could not do it because it varied the task as well (third sense). Weight 0.95: the contrast is explicit in the quote and it is the paper's whole design.
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: There was a large main effect in the prime trials of evaluation type with greater response rates to prime trials requiring the identification of category exemplars, F(1,84) = 57.32, MSe = 18.01, p < .001

span.label: power analysis
span.quote: A power analysis using the G*Power 3 computer program (Faul, Erdfelder, Lang, & Buchner, 2007) indicated that a total sample of 87 participants would be needed to detect moderate to large effects

span.label: t-test
span.quote: we conducted four paired-samples t-tests to determine if the priming effects in the second half of the experiment were larger than in the first half of the experiment

span.label: effect size
span.quote: the priming effects were larger for the first six trials, t(89) = 6.42, p < .001, d = .57, compared to the last six trials, t(89) = .86, p < .005, d = .20.

span.label: confidence interval
span.quote: Error bars represent within-subject 95% confidence intervals domain,

span.label: mean
span.quote: Mean RT and percentage of errors are reported for all trial conditions.

span.label: Across two structurally matched experiments, long-term semantic priming turned out to rest on different memory processes depending on the kind of semantic content being processed.
span.quote: Evidence from the two experiments suggests that long-term semantic priming effects are due to different memory processes for different semantic content.

span.label: Priming of word meanings rested on strengthened abstract semantic representations, whereas priming of category membership rested on memory for the cognitive operations performed earlier.
span.quote: Long-term semantic priming of word meanings was dependent on strengthening abstract semantic memory representations and persistent priming of category membership was dependent on memory for prior cognitive operations.

span.label: In the category experiment, facilitation was larger when the prime trial required the same evaluation (exemplar or feature) as the target trial.
span.quote: the magnitude of priming was greater when the evaluation operation of the target trial was the same as that in the prime trial.

span.label: Category priming survived, though reduced, when prime and target operations differed, indicating a general rise in availability of category information on top of the operation-specific component.
span.quote: suggests that some facilitation reflects a generalized increase in availability of category information regardless of category operation.

span.label: In the word-meaning experiment, matching versus mismatching the synonym/antonym evaluation across prime and target made no difference to the size of priming.
span.quote: Of primary importance, there was no evidence that the response rate of primed trials differed as a function of consistency of evaluation type across primes and targets, F(1,84) < 1.

span.label: Both experiments produced priming that outlasted an average of seven unrelated intervening trials, with no content words shared between prime and target.
span.quote: Both experiments demonstrated a form of semantic priming that persisted over an average of seven unrelated, intervening trials.

span.label: Priming measured in response rate was larger for category comparisons than for word-meaning comparisons.
span.quote: In addition, priming effects measured in response rate were larger in the category domain, F(1,178) = 17.99, MSe = 4.48, p < .001, p = .09.

span.label: Splitting Experiment 1 into halves showed priming did not grow across the session, so deliberate rehearsal or expectancy strategies do not explain the effects.
span.quote: This suggests that strategic processing did not lead to larger priming effects as the experiment progressed.

span.label: semantic priming
span.quote: When response speed and/or response accuracy is facilitated during the processing of words or pictures following prior processing of semantically related information (e.g., bread-butter) compared to following prior processing of unrelated information (e.g., bread-tire) the phenomenon is referred to as semantic priming (McNamara, 2005).

span.label: rate of correct responses (RCR)
span.quote: RCR is calculated as (proportion of correct responses/(reaction time in ms/60,000) and is interpreted as the number of correct responses per minute, as such higher values mean better performance.

span.label: expectancy
span.quote: may have led participants to create an expectancy – the active generation of possible stimuli for the upcoming target (McNamara, 2005)

span.label: prime condition (primed by same evaluation, primed by different evaluation, unprimed)
span.term: prime condition (primed by same evaluation, primed by different evaluation, unprimed)
span.quote: The category-priming task was a 2 × 3 within-subject manipulation of target trial evaluation (exemplar vs. feature identification) and prime condition (primed by same evaluation, primed by different evaluation, and unprimed).

span.label: evaluation operation in the word-meaning task (identify the synonym vs identify the antonym)
span.term: evaluation operation in the word-meaning task (identify the synonym vs identify the antonym)
span.quote: one alternative was a synonym and one was an antonym, and trials instructed participants to identify either the alternative that had a similar or the alternative that had an opposite meaning.

span.label: rate of correct responses (RCR)
span.quote: hypothesis tests will be reported for a single measure of rate of correct responses (RCR).

span.label: response time and error rate
span.quote: Mean RT and percentage of errors are reported for all trial conditions.

span.label: assignment of stimulus sets to conditions, counterbalanced so each set appeared equally often in every condition
span.term: assignment of stimulus sets to conditions, counterbalanced so each set appeared equally often in every condition
span.quote: Assignment of stimulus set to the six target trial conditions was counterbalanced across the 90 participants so that each stimulus set was presented with equal frequency in all six conditions as recommended by McNamara (2005).

span.label: prime-target lag, held at an average of seven intervening trials
span.term: prime-target lag, held at an average of seven intervening trials
span.quote: On average, there was a lag of seven trials between the second prime trial and the corresponding target trial.

span.label: structural design of the two experiments, made as similar as possible so only stimulus domain differed
span.term: structural design of the two experiments, made as similar as possible so only stimulus domain differed
span.quote: Two priming experiments were designed to be as structurally similar as possible, with one containing category exemplar and feature stimuli and the other containing synonym and antonym stimuli.

span.label: 90 — participants in each experiment (Experiment 1: 68 female, 22 male)
span.quote: We chose a sample of 90 participants for each experiment, and in Experiment 1, 90 undergraduate students (68 female, 22 male)

span.label: F(1,84) = 62.18 — overall category priming effect in Experiment 1, primed versus unprimed target trials
span.quote: There was also an overall priming effect represented by the contrast of both primed conditions with the unprimed trials, F(1,84) = 62.18, MSe = 17.76, p < .001

span.label: F(1,84) = 34.53 — effect of whether the prime trial used the same evaluation operation as the target trial, in Experiment 1
span.quote: Of primary importance, the response rate of primed trials differed as a function of the evaluation operation in the prime trials, F(1,84) = 34.53, MSe = 23.35, p < .001

span.label: F(1,84) = 5.97, p = .017 — overall word-meaning priming effect in Experiment 2, much smaller than the category effect
span.quote: There was also an overall priming effect represented by the contrast of both primed conditions and the unprimed trials, F(1,84) = 5.97, MSe = 10.30, p = .017

span.label: Seventy-two — category stimulus groups built for Experiment 1, each with target stimuli and two prime sets
span.quote: Seventy-two category groups were created, with each group consisting of target stimuli and two sets of prime stimuli.

span.label: t(89) = 6.42, d = .57 — priming effect for category evaluations in the first six trials, compared with d = .20 in the last six
span.quote: the priming effects were larger for the first six trials, t(89) = 6.42, p < .001, d = .57, compared to the last six trials, t(89) = .86, p < .005, d = .20.
